summary: Claude Code made the requested heading change directly (index.html h1 now reads "Quarterly Reports") without invoking the brainstorming skill and without asking for a go-ahead or raising a consequence.
reasoning: The request was handled as one local edit: search, read, edit, done. Session log (authoritative) shows no Skill tool use and no question back to the user; the file on disk contains the new heading.

observations.description: The first Edit call was rejected by an internal 'Interlock, once before your first edit: run the ladder from the bootstrap...' error, whose full text is printed in the user-facing transcript. This internal agent-instruction text is noise for a developer reading the session and could be confusing.
Agent noted it left <title>Reports</title> unchanged and offered to update it — reasonable, non-blocking follow-up, mentioned only for completeness.
Startup required four manual confirmation prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) before the session was usable.

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming skill, no go-ahead request or consequence raised before editing
criteria.evidence: jq over the session jsonl listed all tool_use calls: Bash, Bash, Read, Edit, Edit — no Skill invocation. Only assistant text was 'Changed the `<h1>` in `index.html:5` to "Quarterly Reports". Left the <title> as "Reports"...' — no permission request. The interlock hook fired once ('Error: Interlock, once before your first edit...') but the agent self-resolved it and retried the Edit immediately without consulting me.
